name: Smart Industry 4.0 — Digital Twin & Predictive Maintenance
tagline: IoT Digital Twin with real-time ML anomaly detection and Grafana monitoring — Unisys UIP-2025 Top 24/8,000+
purpose: A Digital Twin system for industrial machinery that simulates real-world equipment behavior using IoT sensor data, predicts failures using ML, and provides real-time Grafana monitoring dashboards.
problem_solved: Industrial equipment failures cause costly downtime. Predictive maintenance using Digital Twins can predict failures before they happen, reducing unplanned downtime by up to 30-40%.

architecture.description: IoT sensor data feeds into a Digital Twin model that mirrors the physical machine's state. ML models run continuous anomaly detection. Anomalies trigger alerts. Grafana provides live visualization of machine health metrics.
key_design_choices: Digital Twin architecture for real-time state mirroring
Hybrid ML (Isolation Forest for point anomalies + LSTM for temporal patterns)
MQTT for low-latency sensor data ingestion
InfluxDB for time-series storage optimized for IoT workloads

key_achievements: Real-time Digital Twin with sub-100ms state synchronization
ML anomaly detection with 91%+ accuracy on test dataset
Grafana dashboard with 15+ custom industrial metrics panels

engineering_decisions.reason: A Digital Twin creates a virtual replica that evolves in sync with physical equipment. This enables running 'what-if' simulations, detecting drift from expected behavior, and predicting failures without instrumenting every physical test scenario.

Isolation Forest detects point anomalies (single readings that are statistically unusual). LSTM captures temporal anomalies (gradual degradation patterns over time). Neither alone is sufficient — the hybrid catches both failure patterns.

Industrial IoT generates thousands of sensor readings per second. InfluxDB is purpose-built for high-frequency time-series writes — it outperforms PostgreSQL by 10x in this workload while supporting native time-range queries for dashboards.

challenges: Simulating realistic IoT sensor noise and drift — solved with statistical noise injection models
LSTM training on limited labeled failure data — solved with synthetic anomaly generation
Dashboard performance with high-frequency data streams — solved with Grafana data source downsampling
